html:
SMTO-PSM-0015 — SMTO couldn't confirm the parameter was saved

GUID: 854e852d-51f5-4514-9a50-6553fea88fc6
Slug: parameter-write-failed
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save a parameter but couldn't confirm afterwards whether it was saved. It may have been saved, partly updated, or not saved at all.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu (⋯) and search for the parameter by name. Don't save anything yet. The save may have worked even though SMTO couldn't confirm it, and saving again could create confusion or overwrite it.
  2. If the parameter is there, open it and check its details, selecting Reveal & edit value to see the value. If everything is right, you're done. Seeing the saved details shows whether the earlier save fully went through.
  3. Only if the parameter is missing or its details are wrong, fix it and select Save once. Saving once after checking avoids repeating a change that already happened.

What success looks like

  • Parameter Store shows the parameter with the details you intended, and saving it shows Saved.

If it still fails

  • If saving fails again, stop and select Copy error details, then send them to the person who manages SMTO; the server's storage may be full or read-only. Don't delete the Parameter Store data to clear the error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Parameter Store create could not read back the record it had just written, or a database-discovery create/update raised after entering its write path, so the write's outcome is unconfirmed.

What this means

  • A store write cannot read back its created record, or database-discovery profile save raises an exception after entering its create/update path. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • A store write cannot read back its created record, or database-discovery profile save raises an exception after entering its create/update path.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the exact intended key and revision before assuming the write failed completely.

How to fix it

  • Read the key from Parameter Store (in the Parameter Store editor or via a GET on that key under /api/agent/parameters) to establish whether the write took effect before writing again. Check the Server log and the Parameter Store database at agent_parameters_db_path for storage errors (disk full, read-only, locked); for discovery saves, the 'Failed to save' / 'Failed to update' message names the key and cause. Reconcile the existing entry, then repeat only the part that did not happen.
  • Read the key from Parameter Store to establish whether the write took effect. Restore storage access and reconcile the existing entry before another write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing write is reconciled and supported storage can confirm the intended entry.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
